title: Admin Microtooling Mesh: runtime-safe snippet executor & human-in-loop playlet
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, runtime-safe executor that lets support engineers run audited micro-utilities (snippets/playlets) in the production context with required guardrails. The mesh should allow: 1) registering typed snippet packages, 2) executing with dry-run and safe rollback, 3) human-in-loop confirmation for sensitive actions, 4) opaque parameterization for secrets, and 5) built-in telemetry and provenance for every execution.

Motivation: Current ad-hoc scripts live in multiple repos and runbook docs; we want a consistent UX for on-call and first-line support that is auditable and reversible. This will reduce mean-time-to-repair for common incidents and lower cognitive load for new responders.

Non-goals: This ticket does NOT replace the full Runbook Orchestrator. It focuses on: snippet execution API, a small storefront/catalog UI in the ops console, and the execution SDK used by the support CLI. Integration into the orchestration mesh (canary automation) will be follow-ups.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered: 
- Safety model: opted for a three-tier safety gating (safe/dry-run, staged-with-approval, full-execute) instead of full policy engine initially to keep iteration velocity high.
- Execution surface: prefer sandboxed sidecar execution (WebAssembly runtime prototype) vs. containerized jobs; chose WASM for faster startup and resource isolation but will add a container fallback for actions requiring system-level network transparency.
- Secret handling: avoid passing plaintext secrets to snippets; use a KMS-proxy token approach (see security notes). This increases latency but preserves auditability.

Artifacts: 
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/77681234/Admin+Microtooling+Mesh+Spec
- Design mockups: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cMockups
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/1342
- Telemetry dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/exec-provenance-staging

Acceptance criteria: 
- Support CLI can list/register/unregister snippet packages and request execution with a chosen safety tier.
- All executions produce immutable provenance records: who/what/when/params/result and link to logs.
- Human-approval flow available via console modal and CLI confirmation token.
- Dry-run produces a diff-style output and does not change any production state.
- Benchmarks: cold-start execution (WASM) < 250ms median for trivial snippets, resource-limited execution must be CPU/memory hardened.

Dependencies: KMS proxy integration, console small storefront component, existing telemetry ingestion pipeline.
comments: 2025-02-16 — Kickoff sync: scoped MVP to 'list/register/execute' + provenance. Engineering + Security + Support. Action: Liam to prototype WASM sidecar by 2025-02-22.

2025-02-20 — Prototype update: WASM runner can execute a no-op snippet with sandboxed filesystem; still blocked on KMS proxy for secret injection. See PR #1342 for prototype code and README with run instructions.

2025-02-24 — Security review (informal): recommended adding per-snippet capability declarations (network/disk/time) and rate limits. Decided to add capability declarations to the package manifest v1.1 and enforce via runner. Follow-up security review scheduled.

2025-02-26 — Support team feedback: favored human-approval modal in console and a CLI token fallback for automation. Requested ability to pin 'trusted' snippets from SRE. Added to scope as optional label-based gating.

2025-02-28 — Implementation note: switched from in-process WASM runtime to sidecar to simplify language runtimes and isolation. This increased container count but improved crash isolation; updated cost estimate accordingly.

2025-03-01 — Removed 'full orchestration' requirement from MVP to accelerate delivery; will ship a console storefront and CLI integration first. Next steps: finish KMS proxy integration, implement capability checks, add provenance events to telemetry pipeline.
